questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Lusaka?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Zambia is Lusaka.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Zambia about 752,618 square kilometres; Gabon about 267,667 square kilometres; Eritrea about 117,600 square kilometres; Lesotho about 30,355 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Zambia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Zambia article.

questions.proof: The capital of Zambia is Lusaka, which is also the largest city in the country.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Zambia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Zambia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Zambia article.

questions.proof: It shares its borders with the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the north, Tanzania to the northeast, Malawi to the east, Mozambique to the southeast, Zimbabwe and Botswana (Via a very tiny border) to the south, Namibia (Via the Caprivi Strip) to the southwest, and Angola to the west.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Zambia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Zambia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
